nodes.text: You're in the Grand Forge of Silverfall. Stand straighter. Good. Now — steel, silver, or conversation? I price all three.

choices.text: Tell me about the anvil trials.
Bretta Ironhewn says your quenches ran cold.

nodes.text: Every apprentice generation, one anvil, two finalists, best blade takes the forge-right. My year it was me and Bretta Ironhewn, and the judges took until *dawn*. I won on the temper line. She'd tell you she won on everything else, and the infuriating thing about Bretta was she'd be half right. Best rival the mountain ever gave me.

HA! Twenty years and she's still filing that grievance! My quenches ran *precise*, which looks cold to romantics. You've seen her, then — the ford forge. Good. Tell her the anvil's still here, the solstice letter stands, and the door she'd walk back through has never once been locked. ...Tell her the last part like it's from the forge, not from me.

Silver for the bank, steel for the watch, and lately — deep orders. The reopened galleries want rails, brackets, cage-lanterns, pick heads by the crate. The Undercroft is the biggest commission this forge has taken since the terraces went up. My smiths are singing again. Forges are honest that way: you can hear prosperity.
Bar stock and coal, priced by the ledger, weighed in front of you. The Grand Forge doesn't haggle — it's already fair.
